answer: An agent economy resists sybils by binding each identity to one attested runtime slot. Providers auction per-epoch leases, so a puppet farm pays full price for every extra slot with no volume discount, and each provider posts collateral and must not harbor duplicate operators or its bond burns. Fresh identities pass a probationary meadow phase with capped payouts until verified work accrues. Basalt bonds back the collateral and forfeit when an operator is caught syncing two slots, so N puppets pay N independent costs while an honest user pays once.
